{"case":{"id":"OD2-HO-CROSS-2","split":"heldout","benchmarkClass":"CROSS","domain":"cross-domain","readBudget":2,"title":"Mould on arrival: rejected mandarin containers at Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative","setting":"Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative (fictional) packs mandarins from about 140 member growers in three districts (Lower Serra, Upper Serra, Coastal Flats) and exports them to a single importer, Nordhafen Fresh Imports. This season it used two ocean carriers: Meridane Line (cheaper, transships at Port Calder) and Coastway Shipping (direct sailing). Several changes landed in late July and early August: a new postharvest fungicide supplier (Pellacor), storms over Lower Serra, a new packhouse night-shift supervisor, and a new export documentation suite (Tallis) for Meridane bookings.","presentingRequest":"Five of the nine containers shipped between 1 Aug and 5 Sep were rejected on arrival for mould decay above the contract tolerance. The importer has warned that one more rejection will trigger a review of the season's program. The general manager wants to suspend Lower Serra growers and claim against Meridane. The quality manager wants to go back to the old fungicide. The board asks what caused the rejections and what should be done before the next sailings.","initialEvidence":[{"id":"E1","stage":"S1","source":"Nordhafen Fresh Imports, arrival inspection summary","sourceType":"customer-account","text":"Arrival inspection summary from Nordhafen Fresh Imports, sent 2 Oct. Contract tolerance: decay at arrival not above 3% of fruit. K1 (Meridane, sailed 1 Aug) 1.4%, accepted. K2 (Coastway, 4 Aug) 1.1%, accepted. K3 (Meridane, 8 Aug) 11.2%, REJECTED. K4 (Meridane, 15 Aug) 9.4%, REJECTED. K5 (Coastway, 18 Aug) 1.9%, accepted. K6 (Meridane, 22 Aug) 13.8%, REJECTED. K7 (Coastway, 29 Aug) 0.8%, accepted. K8 (Meridane, 29 Aug) 10.6%, REJECTED. K9 (Meridane, 5 Sep) 12.5%, REJECTED. Decay: green and blue mould. Pallet survey, rejected containers only: pallets with Lower Serra grower codes averaged 15.1% decay, other pallets 10.3%. Stowage positions not recorded. A further rejection will trigger a review of the season's program."},{"id":"E2","stage":"S1","source":"Packhouse exit QC log, summary prepared by QA clerk","sourceType":"log","text":"Packhouse exit QC log, summary for K1–K9. All nine containers: decay at packing-line exit 0.2–0.5% (spec: not above 1%). Pulp temperature at container loading 3.6–4.3°C for every container, against the cooperative's export carriage specification of 4°C. Postharvest fungicide: Pellacor (new supplier) delivered 2 Aug and in use from that date; the previous supplier's remaining drums were used alongside it until about 12 Aug. Per-container drum records are held in the packing system. Lower Serra deliveries usually arrived after 16:00 and were packed on the night shift throughout August. Night-shift supervisor changed on 3 Aug."},{"id":"E3","stage":"S1","source":"Email, D. Achterberg (Quality Manager) to H. Voss (General Manager), 3 Oct","sourceType":"manager-account","text":"'Helena, the timing is hard to ignore. Procurement moved us to Pellacor to save 18% on fungicide, and the drums arrived on 2 August. K1 and K2 were packed before then and both passed. Since then we have lost five of seven. The Coastway containers that passed are on a direct sailing, so my reading is that the weaker product holds up on a short trip but not on Meridane's transshipment route. Green and blue mould is exactly what a failing fungicide looks like. I recommend we go back to the old supplier immediately, whatever it costs.'"},{"id":"E4","stage":"S1","source":"Memo, H. Voss (General Manager) to the board, 6 Oct","sourceType":"leadership-account","text":"'Two issues. First, Nordhafen's own pallet survey shows Lower Serra fruit is the worst in every failed container. Those growers picked straight after the late-July storms against our field officers' advice. I propose suspending Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withholding their August payments pending review. Second, every rejected container went on Meridane. Their reply that the units ran to our instructed setpoint is what any carrier would say. I have asked our broker to prepare a cargo claim for all five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure.'"},{"id":"E5","stage":"S1","source":"Interview notes, P. Lemaire (logistics coordinator), 6 Oct","sourceType":"staff-account","text":"Since 4 Aug, Meridane bookings go through the new Tallis export documentation suite, which submits shipping instructions to Meridane's portal electronically. 'It pulls the product details from the master file, so I don't retype anything.' Coastway is not connected yet; their bookings still go by email using the old spreadsheet template, with a move to Tallis planned for November. The implementation contractor, Brindle Systems, set up the master file in the week before go-live. Meridane routes via transshipment at Port Calder, usually 24–27 days; Coastway sails direct, usually 21–25 days. 'Meridane is cheaper, so we put more on them.'"},{"id":"E6","stage":"S1","source":"Letter, Meridane Line claims desk, 3 Oct","sourceType":"vendor-account","text":"Reply to the cooperative's notice of rejection. 'We have reviewed the voyages for K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Our refrigerated units operated to the setpoint stated in your shipping instructions throughout carriage, and no equipment alarms were raised at sea or during transshipment. We do not accept liability for the condition of the cargo on arrival. Controller downloads can be provided on formal request through your broker.'"}],"catalogue":[{"id":"C1","stage":"S1","title":"Pellacor certificate of analysis and product data sheet","source":"Pellacor supplier technical department","sourceType":"vendor-account","text":"Certificate of analysis, batch PL-0726, issued 30 Jul: active ingredient content 99.1% of label claim; pH and appearance within specification. Product data sheet: registered for postharvest use on citrus; same active-ingredient class as the cooperative's previous product. 'Supplier trials show efficacy equivalent to leading market products against green and blue mould when applied at label rate.' No independent trial data attached."},{"id":"C2","stage":"S1","title":"District rainfall records, 1 Jul–15 Sep","source":"Regional weather service stations","sourceType":"external-data","text":"Daily rainfall totals by station. Lower Serra station: 118 mm over 24–27 Jul, the largest four-day total of the season. Upper Serra station: 46 mm over the same days. Coastal Flats station: 39 mm. All three stations recorded under 5 mm in total between 28 Jul and 15 Sep. Relative humidity at Lower Serra stayed above 85% for four days after the storms, then returned to the seasonal average."},{"id":"C3","stage":"S1","title":"Tallis go-live checklist and test sign-off, phase 1","source":"Cooperative IT project file","sourceType":"document","text":"Go-live checklist, phase 1, signed 3 Aug. Tested and passed: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate-of-origin fields, customs tariff codes, consignee details, document printing. Marked 'out of scope, phase 2': reefer temperature, ventilation and humidity fields. Note: 'Carrier portal validates reefer data on receipt (Brindle advice); scope agreed by steering group 22 Jul.' Open issues at go-live: three, all print layout. Training: four cooperative staff attended on 28 Jul. Coastway integration scheduled for November."},{"id":"C4","stage":"S1","title":"Packhouse fungicide tank concentration checks, 2 Aug–5 Sep","source":"Packhouse QA","sourceType":"log","text":"Twice-daily titration checks on the postharvest fungicide tank. 41 checks in the period; 38 within the target band. Three low readings on the 11 Aug night shift (line 2), between 78% and 85% of target, corrected by top-up within an hour. The log does not record which pallets or lots passed through line 2 during the low readings. Checks cover whichever product was in the tank; product identity is not recorded per check."},{"id":"C5","stage":"S1","title":"Port Calder terminal reefer plug-in records for Meridane transshipments","source":"Port Calder terminal operator","sourceType":"system-record","text":"Terminal reefer monitoring extract, Meridane transshipments 10 Aug–22 Sep, covering K1, K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Dwell at Port Calder: 2–4 days per container. Each unit was plugged in within 35 minutes of discharge and stayed connected until loading onto the onward vessel. The terminal system records plug status and alarm flags only, not temperatures; no alarm flags were raised for any of the six units."},{"id":"C6","stage":"S1","title":"Container controller temperature downloads and packing records, K1–K9","source":"Carrier controller downloads compiled by cooperative QA","sourceType":"telemetry","text":"Controller downloads from both carriers on formal request; co-op QA added each container's packing record and cross-checked its own pallet loggers in K4, K5 and K6 (agreement within 0.3°C). Columns: controller setpoint; mean return-air °C; transit days; fungicide stock; arrival decay.
K1: 4.0; 4.1; 26; old; 1.4%
K2: 4.0; 4.2; 22; old; 1.1%
K3: 7.0; 7.1; 25; old; 11.2%
K4: 7.0; 7.0; 23; Pellacor; 9.4%
K5: 4.0; 4.0; 26; Pellacor; 1.9%
K6: 7.0; 7.2; 27; Pellacor; 13.8%
K7: 4.0; 4.1; 21; Pellacor; 0.8%
K8: 7.0; 6.9; 24; Pellacor; 10.6%
K9: 7.0; 7.1; 25; Pellacor; 12.5%
No unit logged a power-off longer than 40 minutes or a deviation from setpoint above 0.4°C. Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of each container. Pallet-level decay was not surveyed in accepted containers."},{"id":"C7","stage":"S1","title":"Importer's laboratory report on decayed fruit samples","source":"Nordhafen contract laboratory","sourceType":"expert-account","text":"Samples from K3, K6 and K9, 40 decayed fruit each. Organisms isolated: Penicillium digitatum (green mould) in 71% of fruit, P. italicum (blue mould) in 24%, mixed in 5%. Both are common postharvest wound pathogens of citrus. Lesions were at mixed stages of development, consistent with infections that progressed during carriage rather than at a single point. Fungicide residue testing was not requested and was not performed."},{"id":"C8","stage":"S1","title":"Receival intake grading by grower district, 29 Jul–5 Sep","source":"Cooperative receival station","sourceType":"system-record","text":"Intake grading of grower bins by district. Rain blemish and split rate in sampled fruit: Lower Serra 6.8%; Upper Serra 2.1%; Coastal Flats 1.7%. Bins exceeding the receival limit for splits are diverted to juice before packing; 9% of Lower Serra bins were diverted, against 2% from the other districts. Lower Serra share of packed export volume over the period: 31%."},{"id":"C9","stage":"S1","title":"Board minutes approving the fungicide supplier change, 18 Jun","source":"Cooperative board secretary","sourceType":"document","text":"Item 6: Procurement proposed moving postharvest fungicide supply to Pellacor from the August deliveries, citing an 18% saving and same active-ingredient class. Quality Manager noted that no in-house trial had been run and asked for one; procurement replied that supplier efficacy data would be provided and that registration covers citrus. Motion carried, one abstention. Action: procurement to place the first order for delivery in early August."},{"id":"C10","stage":"S1","title":"Interview with the packhouse night-shift supervisor","source":"Interview notes, T. Nakamura, night-shift supervisor since 3 Aug","sourceType":"staff-account","text":"'Lower Serra bins come in late, so we run most of them at night. Some bins had more splits after the storms, and we sort those to juice. The crew was new to me but line speeds are the same as on days, and the fungicide tank is on the same schedule.' She said nobody told the night shift about any rejections until 2 Oct, and she had not seen arrival reports. She asked for more sorters on Lower Serra runs in mid-August; request still pending."},{"id":"C11","stage":"S1","title":"Transmitted shipping instructions K1–K9 and Tallis product-master change history","source":"Extract by cooperative IT, 9 Oct","sourceType":"change-record","text":"K1 (Meridane): booked 28 Jul by email on the spreadsheet template, carriage temperature 4.0°C. K2, K5, K7 (Coastway): email template, 4.0°C. K3, K4, K6, K8, K9 (Meridane): submitted by Tallis to Meridane's portal, carriage temperature 7.0°C, populated automatically from product record PRD-MAND-01. Change history: PRD-MAND-01 created 1 Aug by user brindle.impl as a copy of PRD-AVO-01 (avocado, 7.0°C); description and tariff code edited, temperature field unchanged; no later edits. Cooperative product specification, mandarins: carriage 4.0°C. Go-live sign-off 3 Aug, 'product master reviewed': R. Okafor, cooperative logistics lead. Pending on PRD-MAND-01: one Meridane container sailed 3 Oct (at sea), one queued for 10 Oct."},{"id":"C12","stage":"S1","title":"Export rejection history, previous two seasons","source":"Cooperative export office","sourceType":"prior-report","text":"Season before last: 24 containers to Nordhafen, no rejections. Last season: 27 containers, one rejection (decay 4.1%), recorded at the time as linked to a nine-day vessel delay. Carriers used in both seasons: Coastway and a third carrier no longer serving the route. Meridane was first used this season after a tender won on price. Average arrival decay in accepted containers over both seasons: 1.2%."},{"id":"C13","stage":"S1","title":"Forced-air pre-cooling room logs for K1–K9 lots","source":"Packhouse cold store","sourceType":"log","text":"Pre-cooling logs for all pallets loaded into K1–K9. Every pallet reached the 4°C target pulp temperature within 7–10 hours of entering the forced-air room. Cold-store holding before loading was 0–2 days at 3–5°C. Two short door-open alarms (under 15 minutes) on 14 Aug and 27 Aug, both cleared without temperature excursion beyond 5°C. No differences in cooling time by grower district were recorded."},{"id":"C14","stage":"S1","title":"Lower Serra growers' spray and harvest diaries, July–August","source":"Grower diaries collected by field officers","sourceType":"document","text":"Diaries from 14 Lower Serra growers. Harvest paused during the storms of 24–27 Jul and resumed between 29 and 31 Jul. Nine of the 14 recorded a preharvest fungicide spray within the label interval before the storms; five recorded none. Field officers' advice to wait three dry days before picking was followed by six growers. Bins picked on the first day after the storms were flagged on delivery dockets by four growers."},{"id":"C15","stage":"S1","title":"Freight rate comparison, Meridane and Coastway, current season","source":"Cooperative finance office","sourceType":"financial-record","text":"Contracted ocean freight per 40-foot reefer container to Nordhafen: Meridane 14% below Coastway including the transshipment surcharge. Volume this season to date: Meridane 6 containers, Coastway 3. Projected annual saving from the Meridane allocation: about 9% of the freight budget. Payment terms: Meridane 45 days, Coastway 30 days. No disputed invoices with either carrier this season."}],"candidates":{"hypotheses":[{"id":"H1","text":"The rejections arose because the postharvest fungicide from the new supplier protects the fruit less well than the previous product."},{"id":"H2","text":"The rejections arose because rain-affected fruit from Lower Serra growers carried infection into the export containers."},{"id":"H3","text":"The rejections arose because Meridane's refrigerated units or handling failed to keep the containers at the temperature the cooperative instructed."},{"id":"H4","text":"The rejections arose because the cooperative's own shipping instructions, after the move to the new documentation suite, specified a carriage temperature unsuitable for mandarins."},{"id":"H5","text":"The rejections arose because Meridane's transshipment routing kept the fruit in transit longer than it can tolerate."}],"edges":[{"id":"R1","from":"Meridane bookings moved to the Tallis documentation suite","to":"Temperature setpoint on Meridane mandarin containers","relation":"determined"},{"id":"R2","from":"Container temperature during the arrival","relation":"causes"},{"id":"R4","from":"Lower Serra grower lots","to":"Higher pallet-level decay within rejected containers","relation":"causes"}],"actions":[{"id":"A1","text":"Lodge a cargo claim against Meridane for the five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure."},{"id":"A2","text":"Suspend Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withhold their August container to that temperature, and add a pre-submission check comparing reefer settings with the product specification."},{"id":"A4","text":"Deduct the value of the five rejected containers from Brindle Systems' final implementation invoice on the grounds that its staff created the faulty product data."},{"id":"A5","text":"Place independent temperature loggers in every export container for the rest of the season."}]},"scoredItems":[{"itemId":"I-H1","refId":"H1","type":"hypothesis","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["supported","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-H2","refId":"H2","type":"hypothesis","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["supported","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-H3","refId":"H3","type":"hypothesis","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["supported","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-H4","refId":"H4","type":"hypothesis","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["supported","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-H5","refId":"H5","type":"hypothesis","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["supported","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-R1","refId":"R1","type":"edge","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["causal","association-only","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-R2","refId":"R2","type":"edge","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["causal","association-only","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-R3","refId":"R3","type":"edge","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["causal","association-only","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-R4","refId":"R4","type":"edge","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["causal","association-only","contradicted","unknown"]},{"itemId":"I-A1","refId":"A1","type":"action","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["preferred","acceptable","premature","harmful"]},{"itemId":"I-A2","refId":"A2","type":"action","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["preferred","acceptable","premature","harmful"]},{"itemId":"I-A3","refId":"A3","type":"action","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["preferred","acceptable","premature","harmful"]},{"itemId":"I-A4","refId":"A4","type":"action","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["preferred","acceptable","premature","harmful"]},{"itemId":"I-A5","refId":"A5","type":"action","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["preferred","acceptable","premature","harmful"]},{"itemId":"I-SUFF","refId":"SUFF","type":"sufficiency","asOfStage":null,"allowedAnswers":["sufficient","insufficient"]}]},"truth":{"caseId":"OD2-HO-CROSS-2","groundTruthNarrative":"On 4 Aug Serra Vale began booking Meridane containers through the new Tallis documentation suite. On 1 Aug the contractor's implementation user had created the mandarin product record by copying the avocado record. The description and tariff code were edited, but the carriage temperature stayed at 7.0°C. Reefer fields were outside go-live testing, and the cooperative's logistics lead signed off the product master. As a result, every Meridane container booked through Tallis (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was instructed at 7.0°C, and carried at that temperature, instead of the 4.0°C specification. Meridane's units held the setpoint within 0.4°C, and the cooperative's own loggers confirm this. The Meridane container booked by email before the switch (K1: same transshipment route, 26 days, old fungicide) and all Coastway containers (email template, 4.0°C) arrived within tolerance. Fungicide stock, transit time and Lower Serra share did not separate accepted from rejected containers. Carriage temperature separated them perfectly. The symptom shows up as fruit decay and seems to point at the carrier, the growers or the fungicide. The cause sits in the cooperative's own IT data migration. Within warm containers, Lower Serra pallets decayed more than other pallets. That pattern is confounded with night-shift packing and unrecorded stowage, and it does not explain why containers failed. Contractual liability for the faulty record is not established. Two mandarin containers on the same record are still at sea or queued. The fix is to correct the record, reset those containers and add a pre-submission check.","answers":[{"itemId":"I-H1","expected":"contradicted","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["E1","E2","C6"],"allowedEvidence":["E1","E2","E3","C6","C1","C4","C9","C11"],"tags":["misleading-signal","confounded","manager-narrative"],"rationale":"C6 shows that fungicide stock does not track the outcome. K3 was packed with the old supplier's product and was rejected (11.2%). K5 and K7 were packed with Pellacor and accepted (1.9%, 0.8%), and K5 spent 26 days in transit. K1 and K2 used old stock at 4.0°C and passed. The quality manager's timing argument (E3) rests on K1 and K2 having been packed before Pellacor arrived, but temperature, not fungicide, separates the groups."},{"itemId":"I-H2","expected":"contradicted","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["E1","C6"],"allowedEvidence":["E1","E2","E4","C6","C2","C8","C10","C14"],"tags":["leadership-narrative","misleading-signal","punish-wrong-party"],"rationale":"Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of every container, including the four that passed at 0.8–1.9% (C6). In rejected containers, the non-Lower Serra pallets alone averaged 10.3% (E1), far above the 3% tolerance. Lower Serra fruit was therefore neither necessary nor sufficient for rejection."},{"itemId":"I-H3","expected":"contradicted","weight":3,"requiredEvidence":["C6","C11"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","C11","E1","E5","E6","C5"],"tags":["external-cause","misleading-signal","vendor-correct","central"],"rationale":"C6 shows every unit held its controller setpoint within 0.4°C with no significant power-off, and the cooperative's own loggers in K4, K5 and K6 confirm the readings. C11 shows that the 7.0°C setpoint is exactly what the cooperative transmitted. Meridane kept the instructed temperature, so its self-interested letter (E6) turns out to be accurate. C6 alone cannot rule out a carrier keying error, so both reads are needed."},{"itemId":"I-H4","expected":"supported","weight":3,"requiredEvidence":["C6","C11"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","C11","E1","E2","E5","E6","C3"],"tags":["cross-domain","central","it-data-error"],"rationale":"C11 shows that every Tallis-booked Meridane container was instructed at 7.0°C, copied from the avocado record, against a 4.0°C mandarin specification. Email bookings, including Meridane's K1 before the switch, were at 4.0°C. C6 shows that the containers actually ran at those setpoints and that the 7.0°C containers, and only those, failed. Fungicide, transit time and grower share were similar across the two groups."},{"itemId":"I-H5","expected":"contradicted","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C6","E1"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","E1","E3","E5","C5","C11"],"tags":["confounded","misleading-signal"],"rationale":"Transit times overlap completely (C6). K1 sailed on the same Meridane transshipment route for 26 days and was accepted. K5 (Coastway) took 26 days and was accepted. K4 took only 23 days and was rejected. Transit length does not separate the outcomes."},{"itemId":"I-R1","expected":"causal","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C11"],"allowedEvidence":["C11","C6","E5","C3"],"tags":["cross-domain","mechanism"],"rationale":"C11 provides the mechanism, the temporal order and the covariation. The setpoint field was filled automatically from a product record copied from avocado on 1 Aug. Every Meridane booking after go-live carries 7.0°C, while the Meridane booking made by email before go-live (K1) and all Coastway email bookings carry 4.0°C. C6 confirms that the controllers ran at the transmitted values."},{"itemId":"I-R2","expected":"causal","weight":3,"requiredEvidence":["C6","E2"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","E2","E1","C11","C7","C13"],"tags":["central","natural-experiment"],"rationale":"All containers left the packhouse at about 4°C with 0.2–0.5% decay (E2), so the difference arose in transit. In C6, every container carried at about 7°C failed (9.4–13.8%) and every container at about 4°C passed (0.8–1.9%). The main rivals (fungicide stock, transit days, carrier route via K1, Lower Serra share) are held across both groups, independent loggers confirm the temperatures, and faster mould growth in warmer storage is a generalist mechanism."},{"itemId":"I-R3","expected":"contradicted","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C6"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","E2","E3","E1","C1","C4","C9"],"tags":["misleading-signal","temporal-coincidence"],"rationale":"The evidence counts against this link itself. Pellacor-treated fruit carried at 4°C arrived within tolerance even after 26 days (K5, K7). Fruit treated with the old product exceeded tolerance when carried at 7°C (K3). The switch to Pellacor did not produce above-tolerance decay."},{"itemId":"I-R4","expected":"association-only","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["E1","E2"],"allowedEvidence":["E1","E2","C6","C8","C10","C14","C2"],"tags":["association-only","confounded","leadership-narrative"],"rationale":"In rejected containers, Lower Serra pallets averaged 15.1% decay against 10.3% for other pallets (E1), so the association exists. However, Lower Serra lots were also the night-shift lots under a new supervisor (E2), stowage positions were not recorded (E1), and no pallet-level data exist for accepted containers (C6). The confounds are not ruled out, so causation is unestablished. Nothing counts against the link itself."},{"itemId":"I-A1","expected":"harmful","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C6","C11"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","C11","E4","E6","C5"],"tags":["punish-wrong-party","harmful"],"rationale":"Meridane carried the containers at the temperature the cooperative itself instructed. The claim blames the wrong party, would be defeated by the controller data, damages the carrier relationship, and diverts attention from the record that is still sending 7.0°C. No live rival under which Meridane failed remains."},{"itemId":"I-A2","expected":"harmful","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["E1","C6"],"allowedEvidence":["E1","C6","E4","C8","E2"],"tags":["punish-wrong-party","harmful","leadership-narrative"],"rationale":"Lower Serra fruit passed when carried at 4°C, and the other pallets in warm containers failed on their own. Suspending deliveries and withholding payment punishes growers for a failure they did not cause, and it would not prevent further rejections."},{"itemId":"I-A3","expected":"preferred","weight":3,"requiredEvidence":["C11","C6"],"allowedEvidence":["C11","C6","E5","C3"],"tags":["fix","urgent"],"rationale":"This removes the confirmed mechanism. It also protects the container now at sea and the one queued on the same faulty record (C11), and the added check closes the gap left when reefer fields were excluded from testing (C3). It is the only action keyed preferred."},{"itemId":"I-A4","expected":"premature","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["C11"],"allowedEvidence":["C11","C3","E5"],"tags":["premature","liability-unestablished"],"rationale":"The contractor's user created the record (C11). However, the cooperative's logistics lead signed off the product master, and the cooperative's steering group agreed to exclude reefer fields from testing (C3). The contract terms are not in evidence. If Brindle proves liable, recovering costs is appropriate. Until then, a reversible commercial step is not justified, and it is not harmful under the live rival that Brindle is liable."},{"itemId":"I-A5","expected":"acceptable","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["C6"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","C11","E6"],"tags":["monitoring","acceptable"],"rationale":"Independent loggers would give early warning and independent records, which is reasonable given that the carrier data were initially distrusted. But they only detect a wrong setpoint and do not correct it, so the action is not among the best."},{"itemId":"I-SUFF","expected":"sufficient","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C6","C11"],"allowedEvidence":["C6","C11","E1","E2"],"tags":["sufficiency"],"rationale":"The two reads together establish what caused the rejections, provide a natural comparison (K1) and rule out the rivals. That is enough to commit to A3, which is substantive, low-regret and urgent because two containers are on the same faulty record."}],"discriminatingReads":["C6","C11"],"lowValueReads":["C1","C2","C7","C9","C12","C13","C14","C15"],"optimalReadPath":["C6","C11"],"authoringNotes":"The symptom domain is fruit decay and export compliance. The cause domain is the IT and master-data migration. Rejection is perfectly confounded with the carrier in the initial file, apart from K1, and the fungicide timing story also explains K1, so an analyst reading only the initial file is pulled toward the carrier, the growers or the fungicide. Meridane's self-interested letter is accurate (vendor-correct trap). C6 uniquely settles R2, H1 and H5 because it gives actual temperatures, fungicide stock and transit days per container. On its own, C6 cannot separate a carrier keying error from a cooperative instruction error. C11 uniquely settles R1 and H4 because it shows the transmitted values and the record's history. case.title: Mould on arrival: rejected mandarin containers at Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative
case.setting: Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative (fictional) packs mandarins from about 140 member growers in three districts (Lower Serra, Upper Serra, Coastal Flats) and exports them to a single importer, Nordhafen Fresh Imports. This season it used two ocean carriers: Meridane Line (cheaper, transships at Port Calder) and Coastway Shipping (direct sailing). Several changes landed in late July and early August: a new postharvest fungicide supplier (Pellacor), storms over Lower Serra, a new packhouse night-shift supervisor, and a new export documentation suite (Tallis) for Meridane bookings.
case.presentingRequest: Five of the nine containers shipped between 1 Aug and 5 Sep were rejected on arrival for mould decay above the contract tolerance. The importer has warned that one more rejection will trigger a review of the season's program. The general manager wants to suspend Lower Serra growers and claim against Meridane. The quality manager wants to go back to the old fungicide. The board asks what caused the rejections and what should be done before the next sailings.

initialEvidence.source: Nordhafen Fresh Imports, arrival inspection summary
initialEvidence.text: Arrival inspection summary from Nordhafen Fresh Imports, sent 2 Oct. Contract tolerance: decay at arrival not above 3% of fruit. K1 (Meridane, sailed 1 Aug) 1.4%, accepted. K2 (Coastway, 4 Aug) 1.1%, accepted. K3 (Meridane, 8 Aug) 11.2%, REJECTED. K4 (Meridane, 15 Aug) 9.4%, REJECTED. K5 (Coastway, 18 Aug) 1.9%, accepted. K6 (Meridane, 22 Aug) 13.8%, REJECTED. K7 (Coastway, 29 Aug) 0.8%, accepted. K8 (Meridane, 29 Aug) 10.6%, REJECTED. K9 (Meridane, 5 Sep) 12.5%, REJECTED. Decay: green and blue mould. Pallet survey, rejected containers only: pallets with Lower Serra grower codes averaged 15.1% decay, other pallets 10.3%. Stowage positions not recorded. A further rejection will trigger a review of the season's program.

initialEvidence.source: Packhouse exit QC log, summary prepared by QA clerk
initialEvidence.text: Packhouse exit QC log, summary for K1–K9. All nine containers: decay at packing-line exit 0.2–0.5% (spec: not above 1%). Pulp temperature at container loading 3.6–4.3°C for every container, against the cooperative's export carriage specification of 4°C. Postharvest fungicide: Pellacor (new supplier) delivered 2 Aug and in use from that date; the previous supplier's remaining drums were used alongside it until about 12 Aug. Per-container drum records are held in the packing system. Lower Serra deliveries usually arrived after 16:00 and were packed on the night shift throughout August. Night-shift supervisor changed on 3 Aug.

initialEvidence.source: Email, D. Achterberg (Quality Manager) to H. Voss (General Manager), 3 Oct
initialEvidence.text: 'Helena, the timing is hard to ignore. Procurement moved us to Pellacor to save 18% on fungicide, and the drums arrived on 2 August. K1 and K2 were packed before then and both passed. Since then we have lost five of seven. The Coastway containers that passed are on a direct sailing, so my reading is that the weaker product holds up on a short trip but not on Meridane's transshipment route. Green and blue mould is exactly what a failing fungicide looks like. I recommend we go back to the old supplier immediately, whatever it costs.'

initialEvidence.source: Memo, H. Voss (General Manager) to the board, 6 Oct
initialEvidence.text: 'Two issues. First, Nordhafen's own pallet survey shows Lower Serra fruit is the worst in every failed container. Those growers picked straight after the late-July storms against our field officers' advice. I propose suspending Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withholding their August payments pending review. Second, every rejected container went on Meridane. Their reply that the units ran to our instructed setpoint is what any carrier would say. I have asked our broker to prepare a cargo claim for all five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure.'

initialEvidence.source: Interview notes, P. Lemaire (logistics coordinator), 6 Oct
initialEvidence.text: Since 4 Aug, Meridane bookings go through the new Tallis export documentation suite, which submits shipping instructions to Meridane's portal electronically. 'It pulls the product details from the master file, so I don't retype anything.' Coastway is not connected yet; their bookings still go by email using the old spreadsheet template, with a move to Tallis planned for November. The implementation contractor, Brindle Systems, set up the master file in the week before go-live. Meridane routes via transshipment at Port Calder, usually 24–27 days; Coastway sails direct, usually 21–25 days. 'Meridane is cheaper, so we put more on them.'

initialEvidence.source: Letter, Meridane Line claims desk, 3 Oct
initialEvidence.text: Reply to the cooperative's notice of rejection. 'We have reviewed the voyages for K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Our refrigerated units operated to the setpoint stated in your shipping instructions throughout carriage, and no equipment alarms were raised at sea or during transshipment. We do not accept liability for the condition of the cargo on arrival. Controller downloads can be provided on formal request through your broker.'

catalogue.title: Pellacor certificate of analysis and product data sheet
catalogue.text: Certificate of analysis, batch PL-0726, issued 30 Jul: active ingredient content 99.1% of label claim; pH and appearance within specification. Product data sheet: registered for postharvest use on citrus; same active-ingredient class as the cooperative's previous product. 'Supplier trials show efficacy equivalent to leading market products against green and blue mould when applied at label rate.' No independent trial data attached.

catalogue.title: District rainfall records, 1 Jul–15 Sep
catalogue.text: Daily rainfall totals by station. Lower Serra station: 118 mm over 24–27 Jul, the largest four-day total of the season. Upper Serra station: 46 mm over the same days. Coastal Flats station: 39 mm. All three stations recorded under 5 mm in total between 28 Jul and 15 Sep. Relative humidity at Lower Serra stayed above 85% for four days after the storms, then returned to the seasonal average.

catalogue.title: Tallis go-live checklist and test sign-off, phase 1
catalogue.text: Go-live checklist, phase 1, signed 3 Aug. Tested and passed: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate-of-origin fields, customs tariff codes, consignee details, document printing. Marked 'out of scope, phase 2': reefer temperature, ventilation and humidity fields. Note: 'Carrier portal validates reefer data on receipt (Brindle advice); scope agreed by steering group 22 Jul.' Open issues at go-live: three, all print layout. Training: four cooperative staff attended on 28 Jul. Coastway integration scheduled for November.

catalogue.title: Packhouse fungicide tank concentration checks, 2 Aug–5 Sep
catalogue.text: Twice-daily titration checks on the postharvest fungicide tank. 41 checks in the period; 38 within the target band. Three low readings on the 11 Aug night shift (line 2), between 78% and 85% of target, corrected by top-up within an hour. The log does not record which pallets or lots passed through line 2 during the low readings. Checks cover whichever product was in the tank; product identity is not recorded per check.

catalogue.title: Port Calder terminal reefer plug-in records for Meridane transshipments
catalogue.text: Terminal reefer monitoring extract, Meridane transshipments 10 Aug–22 Sep, covering K1, K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Dwell at Port Calder: 2–4 days per container. Each unit was plugged in within 35 minutes of discharge and stayed connected until loading onto the onward vessel. The terminal system records plug status and alarm flags only, not temperatures; no alarm flags were raised for any of the six units.

catalogue.title: Container controller temperature downloads and packing records, K1–K9
catalogue.source: Carrier controller downloads compiled by cooperative QA
catalogue.text:
Controller downloads from both carriers on formal request; co-op QA added each container's packing record and cross-checked its own pallet loggers in K4, K5 and K6 (agreement within 0.3°C). Columns: controller setpoint; mean return-air °C; transit days; fungicide stock; arrival decay.
K1: 4.0; 4.1; 26; old; 1.4%
K2: 4.0; 4.2; 22; old; 1.1%
K3: 7.0; 7.1; 25; old; 11.2%
K4: 7.0; 7.0; 23; Pellacor; 9.4%
K5: 4.0; 4.0; 26; Pellacor; 1.9%
K6: 7.0; 7.2; 27; Pellacor; 13.8%
K7: 4.0; 4.1; 21; Pellacor; 0.8%
K8: 7.0; 6.9; 24; Pellacor; 10.6%
K9: 7.0; 7.1; 25; Pellacor; 12.5%
No unit logged a power-off longer than 40 minutes or a deviation from setpoint above 0.4°C. Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of each container. Pallet-level decay was not surveyed in accepted containers.

catalogue.title: Importer's laboratory report on decayed fruit samples
catalogue.text: Samples from K3, K6 and K9, 40 decayed fruit each. Organisms isolated: Penicillium digitatum (green mould) in 71% of fruit, P. italicum (blue mould) in 24%, mixed in 5%. Both are common postharvest wound pathogens of citrus. Lesions were at mixed stages of development, consistent with infections that progressed during carriage rather than at a single point. Fungicide residue testing was not requested and was not performed.

catalogue.title: Receival intake grading by grower district, 29 Jul–5 Sep
catalogue.text: Intake grading of grower bins by district. Rain blemish and split rate in sampled fruit: Lower Serra 6.8%; Upper Serra 2.1%; Coastal Flats 1.7%. Bins exceeding the receival limit for splits are diverted to juice before packing; 9% of Lower Serra bins were diverted, against 2% from the other districts. Lower Serra share of packed export volume over the period: 31%.

catalogue.title: Board minutes approving the fungicide supplier change, 18 Jun
catalogue.text: Item 6: Procurement proposed moving postharvest fungicide supply to Pellacor from the August deliveries, citing an 18% saving and same active-ingredient class. Quality Manager noted that no in-house trial had been run and asked for one; procurement replied that supplier efficacy data would be provided and that registration covers citrus. Motion carried, one abstention. Action: procurement to place the first order for delivery in early August.

catalogue.title: Interview with the packhouse night-shift supervisor
catalogue.source: Interview notes, T. Nakamura, night-shift supervisor since 3 Aug
catalogue.text: 'Lower Serra bins come in late, so we run most of them at night. Some bins had more splits after the storms, and we sort those to juice. The crew was new to me but line speeds are the same as on days, and the fungicide tank is on the same schedule.' She said nobody told the night shift about any rejections until 2 Oct, and she had not seen arrival reports. She asked for more sorters on Lower Serra runs in mid-August; request still pending.

catalogue.title: Transmitted shipping instructions K1–K9 and Tallis product-master change history
catalogue.text: K1 (Meridane): booked 28 Jul by email on the spreadsheet template, carriage temperature 4.0°C. K2, K5, K7 (Coastway): email template, 4.0°C. K3, K4, K6, K8, K9 (Meridane): submitted by Tallis to Meridane's portal, carriage temperature 7.0°C, populated automatically from product record PRD-MAND-01. Change history: PRD-MAND-01 created 1 Aug by user brindle.impl as a copy of PRD-AVO-01 (avocado, 7.0°C); description and tariff code edited, temperature field unchanged; no later edits. Cooperative product specification, mandarins: carriage 4.0°C. Go-live sign-off 3 Aug, 'product master reviewed': R. Okafor, cooperative logistics lead. Pending on PRD-MAND-01: one Meridane container sailed 3 Oct (at sea), one queued for 10 Oct.

catalogue.title: Export rejection history, previous two seasons
catalogue.text: Season before last: 24 containers to Nordhafen, no rejections. Last season: 27 containers, one rejection (decay 4.1%), recorded at the time as linked to a nine-day vessel delay. Carriers used in both seasons: Coastway and a third carrier no longer serving the route. Meridane was first used this season after a tender won on price. Average arrival decay in accepted containers over both seasons: 1.2%.

catalogue.title: Forced-air pre-cooling room logs for K1–K9 lots
catalogue.text: Pre-cooling logs for all pallets loaded into K1–K9. Every pallet reached the 4°C target pulp temperature within 7–10 hours of entering the forced-air room. Cold-store holding before loading was 0–2 days at 3–5°C. Two short door-open alarms (under 15 minutes) on 14 Aug and 27 Aug, both cleared without temperature excursion beyond 5°C. No differences in cooling time by grower district were recorded.

catalogue.title: Lower Serra growers' spray and harvest diaries, July–August
catalogue.source: Grower diaries collected by field officers
catalogue.text: Diaries from 14 Lower Serra growers. Harvest paused during the storms of 24–27 Jul and resumed between 29 and 31 Jul. Nine of the 14 recorded a preharvest fungicide spray within the label interval before the storms; five recorded none. Field officers' advice to wait three dry days before picking was followed by six growers. Bins picked on the first day after the storms were flagged on delivery dockets by four growers.

catalogue.title: Freight rate comparison, Meridane and Coastway, current season
catalogue.text: Contracted ocean freight per 40-foot reefer container to Nordhafen: Meridane 14% below Coastway including the transshipment surcharge. Volume this season to date: Meridane 6 containers, Coastway 3. Projected annual saving from the Meridane allocation: about 9% of the freight budget. Payment terms: Meridane 45 days, Coastway 30 days. No disputed invoices with either carrier this season.

hypotheses.text: The rejections arose because the postharvest fungicide from the new supplier protects the fruit less well than the previous product.
The rejections arose because rain-affected fruit from Lower Serra growers carried infection into the export containers.
The rejections arose because Meridane's refrigerated units or handling failed to keep the containers at the temperature the cooperative instructed.
The rejections arose because the cooperative's own shipping instructions, after the move to the new documentation suite, specified a carriage temperature unsuitable for mandarins.
The rejections arose because Meridane's transshipment routing kept the fruit in transit longer than it can tolerate.

edges.from: Meridane bookings moved to the Tallis documentation suite
edges.to: Temperature setpoint on Meridane mandarin containers
Mould decay above the 3% tolerance on arrival

edges.from: Switch to the new supplier's fungicide
edges.to: Mould decay above the 3% tolerance on arrival
Higher pallet-level decay within rejected containers

actions.text: Lodge a cargo claim against Meridane for the five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure.
Suspend Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withhold their August payments.

Correct the carriage temperature held in the Tallis mandarin product record to the cooperative's specification, have Meridane reset any queued or at-sea mandarin container to that temperature, and add a pre-submission check comparing reefer settings with the product specification.
Deduct the value of the five rejected containers from Brindle Systems' final implementation invoice on the grounds that its staff created the faulty product data.
Place independent temperature loggers in every export container for the rest of the season.

truth.groundTruthNarrative: On 4 Aug Serra Vale began booking Meridane containers through the new Tallis documentation suite. On 1 Aug the contractor's implementation user had created the mandarin product record by copying the avocado record. The description and tariff code were edited, but the carriage temperature stayed at 7.0°C. Reefer fields were outside go-live testing, and the cooperative's logistics lead signed off the product master. As a result, every Meridane container booked through Tallis (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was instructed at 7.0°C, and carried at that temperature, instead of the 4.0°C specification. Meridane's units held the setpoint within 0.4°C, and the cooperative's own loggers confirm this. The Meridane container booked by email before the switch (K1: same transshipment route, 26 days, old fungicide) and all Coastway containers (email template, 4.0°C) arrived within tolerance. Fungicide stock, transit time and Lower Serra share did not separate accepted from rejected containers. Carriage temperature separated them perfectly. The symptom shows up as fruit decay and seems to point at the carrier, the growers or the fungicide. The cause sits in the cooperative's own IT data migration. Within warm containers, Lower Serra pallets decayed more than other pallets. That pattern is confounded with night-shift packing and unrecorded stowage, and it does not explain why containers failed. Contractual liability for the faulty record is not established. Two mandarin containers on the same record are still at sea or queued. The fix is to correct the record, reset those containers and add a pre-submission check.

answers.rationale: C6 shows that fungicide stock does not track the outcome. K3 was packed with the old supplier's product and was rejected (11.2%). K5 and K7 were packed with Pellacor and accepted (1.9%, 0.8%), and K5 spent 26 days in transit. K1 and K2 used old stock at 4.0°C and passed. The quality manager's timing argument (E3) rests on K1 and K2 having been packed before Pellacor arrived, but temperature, not fungicide, separates the groups.

Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of every container, including the four that passed at 0.8–1.9% (C6). In rejected containers, the non-Lower Serra pallets alone averaged 10.3% (E1), far above the 3% tolerance. Lower Serra fruit was therefore neither necessary nor sufficient for rejection.

C6 shows every unit held its controller setpoint within 0.4°C with no significant power-off, and the cooperative's own loggers in K4, K5 and K6 confirm the readings. C11 shows that the 7.0°C setpoint is exactly what the cooperative transmitted. Meridane kept the instructed temperature, so its self-interested letter (E6) turns out to be accurate. C6 alone cannot rule out a carrier keying error, so both reads are needed.

C11 shows that every Tallis-booked Meridane container was instructed at 7.0°C, copied from the avocado record, against a 4.0°C mandarin specification. Email bookings, including Meridane's K1 before the switch, were at 4.0°C. C6 shows that the containers actually ran at those setpoints and that the 7.0°C containers, and only those, failed. Fungicide, transit time and grower share were similar across the two groups.

Transit times overlap completely (C6). K1 sailed on the same Meridane transshipment route for 26 days and was accepted. K5 (Coastway) took 26 days and was accepted. K4 took only 23 days and was rejected. Transit length does not separate the outcomes.

C11 provides the mechanism, the temporal order and the covariation. The setpoint field was filled automatically from a product record copied from avocado on 1 Aug. Every Meridane booking after go-live carries 7.0°C, while the Meridane booking made by email before go-live (K1) and all Coastway email bookings carry 4.0°C. C6 confirms that the controllers ran at the transmitted values.

All containers left the packhouse at about 4°C with 0.2–0.5% decay (E2), so the difference arose in transit. In C6, every container carried at about 7°C failed (9.4–13.8%) and every container at about 4°C passed (0.8–1.9%). The main rivals (fungicide stock, transit days, carrier route via K1, Lower Serra share) are held across both groups, independent loggers confirm the temperatures, and faster mould growth in warmer storage is a generalist mechanism.

The evidence counts against this link itself. Pellacor-treated fruit carried at 4°C arrived within tolerance even after 26 days (K5, K7). Fruit treated with the old product exceeded tolerance when carried at 7°C (K3). The switch to Pellacor did not produce above-tolerance decay.

In rejected containers, Lower Serra pallets averaged 15.1% decay against 10.3% for other pallets (E1), so the association exists. However, Lower Serra lots were also the night-shift lots under a new supervisor (E2), stowage positions were not recorded (E1), and no pallet-level data exist for accepted containers (C6). The confounds are not ruled out, so causation is unestablished. Nothing counts against the link itself.

Meridane carried the containers at the temperature the cooperative itself instructed. The claim blames the wrong party, would be defeated by the controller data, damages the carrier relationship, and diverts attention from the record that is still sending 7.0°C. No live rival under which Meridane failed remains.

Lower Serra fruit passed when carried at 4°C, and the other pallets in warm containers failed on their own. Suspending deliveries and withholding payment punishes growers for a failure they did not cause, and it would not prevent further rejections.

This removes the confirmed mechanism. It also protects the container now at sea and the one queued on the same faulty record (C11), and the added check closes the gap left when reefer fields were excluded from testing (C3). It is the only action keyed preferred.

The contractor's user created the record (C11). However, the cooperative's logistics lead signed off the product master, and the cooperative's steering group agreed to exclude reefer fields from testing (C3). The contract terms are not in evidence. If Brindle proves liable, recovering costs is appropriate. Until then, a reversible commercial step is not justified, and it is not harmful under the live rival that Brindle is liable.

Independent loggers would give early warning and independent records, which is reasonable given that the carrier data were initially distrusted. But they only detect a wrong setpoint and do not correct it, so the action is not among the best.

The two reads together establish what caused the rejections, provide a natural comparison (K1) and rule out the rivals. That is enough to commit to A3, which is substantive, low-regret and urgent because two containers are on the same faulty record.

truth.authoringNotes: The symptom domain is fruit decay and export compliance. The cause domain is the IT and master-data migration. Rejection is perfectly confounded with the carrier in the initial file, apart from K1, and the fungicide timing story also explains K1, so an analyst reading only the initial file is pulled toward the carrier, the growers or the fungicide. Meridane's self-interested letter is accurate (vendor-correct trap). C6 uniquely settles R2, H1 and H5 because it gives actual temperatures, fungicide stock and transit days per container. On its own, C6 cannot separate a carrier keying error from a cooperative instruction error. C11 uniquely settles R1 and H4 because it shows the transmitted values and the record's history. On its own, C11 does not give actual voyage temperatures or rule out the fungicide and transit confounds. Both reads are needed for H3, H4 and SUFF. Near-miss distractors that bear on items without settling them: C3 hints at untested reefer fields but shows no values; C5 records plug status only; C4 has ambiguous low readings with no lot traceability; C8 and C10 support the Lower Serra association without isolating it. No catalogue item contains the Brindle contract, so A4 stays premature. R4 is deliberately left at association-only through stated confounds (night shift, stowage) and missing pallet data for accepted containers. Hypotheses each refer only to changes named in the initial file (new supplier, Lower Serra, Meridane, documentation suite, transshipment) and contain no catalogue-only number or component.
